edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adolescents or adults with eating disorders
edges.mechanism: In eating disorders, DBT aims to reduce impulsive or affect-driven episodes by improving emotion regulation rather than by focusing only on food rules.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2025 Avila-Parcet rct in BMC Psychiatry already points to dialectical behaviour therapy tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
